overviewHtml:
Workflows often need to act differently depending on what a query returns, and it is not obvious how to evaluate a DQL result in a condition.

What you get

  • Two example workflows that branch on error counts per Kubernetes namespace
  • A version that parses the DQL result in a JavaScript task before branching
  • A shorter conditions-only version with no JavaScript task
  • Self-generated test data, so no connections or apps are needed
prereqsHtml:
• Dynatrace SaaS with Workflows
  • No connections or external apps. The DQL query generates its own test data.
setupHtml:
1. Download one of the workflows. Each comes in two formats:
  • *.workflow-template.yaml: workflow template. Import it in Workflows with Upload.
  • *.workflow.json: JSON export for the Automation API.
  1. Import it and choose Run. The workflow uses the on-demand trigger.
  2. Open the execution to see which branch ran.
getStartedHtml:
You only need Dynatrace Workflows.

  1. Download one of the workflows and upload it in Workflows
  2. Run it on demand
  3. Open the execution to see which branch ran
